newsitem.title: UK: Straight-run fuel oil steady in pre-Easter doldrum.
newsitem.headline: Straight-run fuel oil steady in pre-Easter doldrum.

text.p: NWE straight-run fuel prices remained steady on Wednesday in a market becalmed by the approach of the Easter break, traders said.
Bids for most commonly traded low sulphur straight-run in Europe were again around $101-$102 with offers at the $106 level. Sellers appeared to be in no rush to move stock.
The only business seen done was three small batches of mainland European low sulphur material, totalling 20,000 tonnes, sold inland at a price heard to be above 105 fob.
Some 250,000 tonnes of high sulphur Russian material coming out of the Black Sea were heard looking for homes and weighing on prices in the Mediterranean.
Three cargoes of 50,000 tonnes were due to leave the Black Sea before April 1, one trader said, with their destinations unknown.
Traders said the material was originally destined for Italian refineries that are going into maintenance. -- London newsroom +44 171 542 8060
